metadata.note: A CLI-explainer weekly recap -- a NEW week's log, separate from the earlier recaps (weekly-recap-real-art and before). Same story spine as those builds (B00 cold open with intro -> ask -> code -> output x4 -> change -> code -> output -> closing line -> handoff -> outro; real code shown via ClaudeCodeBeat; one required revision cycle). The PROBLEM beat of the earlier recaps is dropped so the whole recap stays under the user's 3-minute limit. weekly_recap_v1.py and weekly_recap_v2.py are genuine Python scripts, both actually run; v1 is a flat list of four parts, v2 adds a STATUS to each (published / produced / attended / ongoing) and prints a done-vs-ongoing count ('3 parts done, 1 ongoing') -- chosen because the user asked for an honest update and the Homes of Hope work is ongoing. THE HOMES OF HOPE WORK IS NOT DESCRIBED beyond 'promotion and outreach with Yatra, ongoing' (user instruction), and the graphic carries the user's required label, 'Homes of Hope documentary outreach (with Yatra)'. HOMES OF HOPE VISUALS ARE ABSTRACT: connected dots around a megaphone, no photos, no children, no people shapes. NO real platform or company logos: the Substack article is a mock header (text kicker, a generic search bar and chat bubble), the meeting is a generic calendar icon. Video count: the user's kickoff says 'two videos ... four files in total'; this recap uses that wording. PACING: the user asked for about 30 to 40 seconds per part and about 3 minutes in total; parts one and two use their full allotment, but parts three and four are short by content (the user's own summaries are two to three sentences, and part four may give no detail beyond 'ongoing'), so they run about 14 and 20 seconds rather than being padded -- the whole recap is well under 3 minutes. Disclosed substitutions carried forward: (1) af_bella + @HumanitariansAI instead of the skill's default voice/handle; (2) rendered through run.sh/compile.py/static_scene_check.py/manim_layout_audit.py/final_frame_check.py. Self-intro ('Hi, I'm Agrima') opens B00's narration per the user's kickoff. All items are the user's own self-reported account. No footage exists -- every visual is a generated Manim graphic.

props.title: weekly_recap_v1.py
props.code:
WEEK = [
    {"part": "1. Writing",
     "item": "Published my weekly article on Substack: 'We Ask the AI Now'"},
    {"part": "2. Video production",
     "item": "Two Brutalist videos (AI topic + weekly recap), each in 16:9 and 9:16: four files"},
    {"part": "3. Weekly meeting",
     "item": "Attended the weekly team meeting"},
    {"part": "4. Homes of Hope",
     "item": "Continued my work on the documentary project with Yatra"},
]


def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"- {entry['part']}: {entry['item']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    log()

beats.role_note: part 1: the 'We Ask the AI Now' article and its summary -- SHOW
beats.narration_text: Run it, and here's the week. Part one, writing. I published my weekly article on Substack: We Ask the AI Now. People aren't leaving search engines. They're splitting their questions between search and AI. Most still use search as their default tool, but many turn to AI chat to explain hard topics, give step-by-step help, brainstorm, and plan trips. Search now shows AI answers at the top, and AI tools now search, so the two are blending. Younger people lead the shift, and people use AI with some doubt. The takeaway: clear, helpful information matters more than ever for being found.
beats.visual_intent: a mock article header for 'We Ask the AI Now' with a generic search bar and chat bubble, a 'published' chip, and the summary as six short chips that appear on the narration; labelled as a mock header

beats.role_note: part 2: two videos x two formats = four files; prompt, plan approval, final check -- SHOW
beats.narration_text: Part two, video production. I made videos with Brutalist, our video-creation tool: an AI topic video based on this article, and this weekly recap. Each was exported in sixteen by nine and nine by sixteen, for four files in total. For each video, I wrote the prompt, reviewed and approved the plan, and checked the final result.
beats.visual_intent: two video rows (AI topic video, weekly recap), each split into a 16:9 and a 9:16 file tile, a '4 video files' count, and three process chips (I wrote the prompt, I reviewed and approved the plan, I checked the final result)

My work with Yatra focuses on promotion and outreach, to help the girls' stories reach a wider audience. That work is ongoing.

props.title: weekly_recap_v2.py
props.code:
WEEK = [
    {"status": "published", "part": "1. Writing",
     "item": "Substack article: 'We Ask the AI Now'"},
    {"status": "produced", "part": "2. Video production",
     "item": "Two Brutalist videos, each in 16:9 and 9:16: four files"},
    {"status": "attended", "part": "3. Weekly meeting",
     "item": "Weekly team meeting"},
    {"status": "ongoing", "part": "4. Homes of Hope",
     "item": "Promotion and outreach, with Yatra"},
]


def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"[{entry['status'].upper()}] {entry['part']}: {entry['item']}")
    ongoing = [e for e in WEEK if e["status"] == "ongoing"]
    print(f"{len(WEEK) - len(ongoing)} parts done, {len(ongoing)} ongoing")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    log()
